analysis.title: Americas Technology: Semiconductors - At the center of tensions around the AI datacenter build: Searching for value following the sector-wide pullback
key_insights: SOX fell 13% in the past week and 31% since Oct. 1 after the Nov. 3 US elections raised doubts about the pace of datacenter builds in states such as Texas. GS calls the sector oversold and sees compelling risk/reward in select names, though it admits few catalysts before year end.

GS frames two tensions for semis: how the gap between hyperscaler/AI lab capex and free cash flow gets closed, and whether enough land, power and shell is coming online to match Street semi estimates. The election put the second one in focus.

GS's bottom-up build implies AI infrastructure capex of about $1.3tn in 2027 (+60% YoY) and $2.0tn in 2028 (+42% YoY). That equates to roughly 20/35/57 GW of AI datacenter deployments in 2026/27/28. The figure covers AI labs, sovereign AI and enterprise buyers as well as hyperscalers.

Per-GW revenue assumptions: Broadcom guides to 10GW in FY27 and 20GW in FY28 at $20-30bn per GW. Nvidia's Blackwell is about $25bn per GW, rising to about $40bn for Rubin (GS adds $5bn for Feynman, about $45bn). AMD outlines $15-20bn per GW, and GS uses the midpoint.

GS sees about 35 GW of 2027 datacenter builds as relatively low risk. For 2028 it sees a 35 GW floor, rising to 55-60 GW if construction projects proceed. Bear Case #2 is 35 GW, Bear Case #1 is 45 GW, the base case is 57 GW and the bull case is 65 GW.

Aterio data on capacity already under construction gives US net additions of 22/24/5 GW-IT for 2027/28/29, against GS forecasts of 20/24/23 GW-IT. GS says its forecasts have likely been below consensus.

Texas is 20% of 2027E and 27% of 2028E net additions among under-construction capacity, and 26% of 2026-30 cumulative net additions. The Governor-elect has called for an immediate moratorium on data centers. GS says moratoria are not bans or cancellations, would likely apply to new projects rather than those under construction, and mainly risk delays and higher costs.

SOX's drawdown relative to the S&P 500 is approaching 30 points, a ten-year record. It has exceeded 20 points on only two prior occasions. Past drawdowns of this size were typically followed by outperformance, so GS sees an index-level entry point. It warns resolution may take time given year-end de-grossing.
AI Compute: GS favors NVDA and AVGO, which trade at 12X/13X a 2028 'no growth' baseline built on 2027 estimates. AMD is very attractive on growth but at a less compelling valuation.

Semi Cap Equipment: GS treats 2027 WFE as a baseline and prefers AMAT and LRCX at 15X/16X 2027E EPS, with Tokyo Electron also screening attractive. Its scenarios assume 2028 WFE growth of about 30%, about 15% and flat.

Memory: global memory stocks have historically bottomed near tangible book value. Samsung and SK Hynix are approaching that level and are already below total book. GS sees improving risk/reward for Neutral-rated Micron given a high probability of strong FCF in coming quarters, and projects Micron could trade significantly below tangible book over upcoming quarters on its FCF estimates.

Rating and target changes in the target history tables: AMD target $675 (was $700 on 5 Oct), AMAT $670, AVGO $540, LRCX $380, NVDA $300, MU $1,250, KLAC $195 (Neutral), TER $440. Marvell is Not Rated because GS is advising on a strategic matter involving it.

market_movers.rationale: Favored AI compute name. Trades at about 12X a 2028 no-growth baseline built on GS's low-risk 35 GW 2027 estimate. 12-month target is 30X normalized EPS of $10.00.
Favored alongside NVDA at about 13X the no-growth baseline. Target is 30X normalized EPS of $18.00. Company guides to 10GW and 20GW of AI deployments in FY27 and FY28.
Very attractive on achievable growth but at a less compelling valuation than NVDA and AVGO. Target is 30X normalized EPS of $22.50.
Preferred semi cap name at 15X-16X 2027E EPS, attractive even with no capex growth beyond 2027. Target is 32X normalized EPS of $21.00. Buy on Conviction List.
Preferred semi cap name alongside AMAT on 2027 WFE as a baseline. Target is 35X normalized EPS of $10.75.
Neutral. Target is 30X normalized EPS of $6.50. Risks include foundry/logic spending and export restrictions.
Risk/reward is becoming more attractive on a high probability of strong FCF in coming quarters. Shares are approaching tangible book value. Target is 18X normalized EPS of $70.00.
Target is 35X normalized EPS of $12.50. Risks include delays in a merchant GPU customer ramp and lumpy AI project revenue.
Samsung Electronics (common). Trading below total book value. EV/EBITDA-based SOTP target. Preference shares target W380,000. Covered by Giuni Lee.
SK Hynix. Trading below total book value. Target is 7.0X 2026E/27E average P/E. Covered by Giuni Lee.
Tokyo Electron. Screens attractive across WFE scenarios. Target uses an 18X sector EV/EBITDA multiple plus a 30% premium. Covered by Shuhei Nakamura.
MediaTek. Target is 25x P/E on 2H27E-1H28E EPS. Covered by Allen Chang. ASIC datacenter revenue forecast to reach $52.5bn in 2028.

sector_views.rationale: NVDA and AVGO trade at 12X/13X a 2028 no-growth baseline. 35 GW of 2027 deployments are largely in progress.
Capacity coming online through 2028 is catching up to past demand. AMAT and LRCX are compelling even with no capex increase beyond 2027.
Stocks are approaching tangible book value, which has historically marked bottoms. Samsung and SK Hynix are Buy-rated and Micron is Neutral.

earnings_insights: Micron (Neutral): GS expects strong FCF in coming quarters, which could push tangible book value well above the share price. GS target uses normalized EPS estimate of $70.00 (GS estimate, not a reported figure).
GS normalized EPS estimates used for targets (estimates, not reported): NVDA $10.00, AVGO $18.00, AMD $22.50, AMAT $21.00, LRCX $10.75, KLAC $6.50, TER $12.50.

GS semi cap scenario analysis uses calendar 2028 EPS estimates that assume about 30% WFE growth (scenario 1), about 15% (scenario 2) and flat WFE on 2027 EPS (scenario 3). These are GS forecasts, not reported figures.

trade_ideas.description: Own NVDA and AVGO (Buy), which trade at 12X/13X a 2028 no-growth baseline
trade_ideas.rationale: The 35 GW of 2027 deployments carries low execution risk, and both stocks look attractive across all downside scenarios.
trade_ideas.risk: Slowdown in AI infrastructure spending, share erosion or competition, and supply constraints.

trade_ideas.description: Own AMAT and LRCX (Buy), which trade at 15X/16X 2027E EPS
trade_ideas.rationale: Equipment capacity through 2028 is catching up to past demand, so 2027 WFE is a baseline.
trade_ideas.risk: Incremental export restrictions, China-based supplier share gains, softer DRAM/HBM demand and delays to fab expansions.

trade_ideas.description: Own AMD (Buy) for growth, at a less compelling valuation than NVDA and AVGO
trade_ideas.rationale: GS finds AMD very attractive given the growth it believes it can achieve.
trade_ideas.risk: Slower agentic AI adoption, slower Meta-related GPU deployment, x86 share erosion and lack of operating leverage.

risk_factors: Datacenter moratoria in Texas could delay ready-for-service dates and raise costs for operators.
Announced but not yet under-construction capacity is the key driver of 2028 upside and 2029-30 growth, and it carries higher risk.
The funding gap between current capex and free cash flow at hyperscalers and AI labs is unresolved.
Year-end de-grossing may keep pressure on semis despite oversold levels, and GS sees few catalysts before year end.
Export restrictions, CXMT competition in DRAM and a prolonged inventory adjustment in semis.

vol_and_positioning: SOX drawdown relative to the S&P 500 is approaching 30 points, a ten-year record, with only two prior instances above 20 points.
GS notes significant de-grossing in the broader market, particularly around year end, which may delay any rebound in semis.
geopolitical: Texas Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa has called for an immediate moratorium on data centers following the Nov. 3 US elections.
Incremental US export restrictions on semiconductors and China-based supplier share gains are cited as risks for AMAT and KLAC.
CXMT gaining DRAM market share is cited as a risk to Micron's pricing.

tension_points.bull_case: GS sees about 35 GW of 2027 deployments as largely in progress and low risk. Under-construction capacity gives US net additions of 22/24/5 GW-IT for 2027/28/29, in line with GS forecasts of 20/24/23. NVDA/AVGO trade at 12X/13X a no-growth 2028 baseline.
tension_points.bear_case: Texas is 20% of 2027E and 27% of 2028E under-construction net additions, and the Governor-elect wants an immediate moratorium. 2028 upside above the 35 GW floor depends on announced but not yet under-construction capacity, which carries higher risk. Delays and higher costs are the main risks.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The report assumes moratoria would apply to new data centers rather than those under construction. A moratorium reaching projects already under construction would undercut the low-risk 35 GW base.

tension_points.bull_case: Street semi estimates are supported by $1.3tn/$2tn of AI infrastructure capex in 2027/28 spanning hyperscalers, AI labs, sovereign AI and enterprise customers.
tension_points.bear_case: It is unclear how the gap between current capex and free cash flow at hyperscalers and AI model labs gets closed.

tension_points.bull_case: SOX drawdown relative to the S&P 500 is a ten-year record near 30 points. Past drawdowns of this size were typically followed by outperformance.
tension_points.bear_case: Resolution may take time given few catalysts before year end and significant de-grossing in the broader market.
